sections.content: How many people are "sports coaches, instructors and officials"?

56,790 people

were counted on the census as "sports coaches, instructors and officials" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Sports coaches, instructors and officials work with amateur and professional sportsmen and women to enhance performance. They also encourage greater participation in sport, supervise recreational activities such as canoeing and mountaineering, and organise and officiate at sporting events.

People who had this job were generally younger

The occupation of "sports coaches, instructors and officials" had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "sports coaches, instructors and officials", 16.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "sports coaches, instructors and officials" was 65 years or older.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "sports coaches, instructors and officials" included:

  • elementary construction occupations (other)
  • telephone salespersons
  • customer service occupations (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "sports coaches, instructors and officials" there were more men than women (57.3% compared with 42.7%).

This means "sports coaches, instructors and officials" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "culture, media and sports occupations".

Men made up 57.3% and women made up 42.7% of "sports coaches, instructors and officials"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "sports coaches, instructors and officials" included:

  • quality assurance technicians
  • shopkeepers and owners - retail and wholesale
  • ambulance staff (excluding paramedics)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "sports coaches, instructors and officials" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "sports coaches, instructors and officials" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "sports coaches, instructors and officials", 7.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (61.4% compared with 38.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (65%) than self-employed (35%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Buckinghamshire, this is in the same region of the South East.
